title: kith-jmap: tests for resolver and error formatting
description:
Tests for ResultReference resolver and JMAP error response formatting.

What: Write the test suite for KITH-2cs (resolver) and KITH-bdp (error formatting) with external oracles from RFC 8620.

Algorithm:
1. Resolver tests (oracles from RFC 8620 §9 and RFC 6901 §5):
   - Construct invocations manually: first call returns known JSON value, second call has '#ids' ResultReference pointing to '/list/*/id'
   - Verify resolve_references transforms the second invocation's args correctly
   - Test: simple path /list/0/id resolves to first element's id
   - Test: path to nonexistent array index → Err
   - Test: path to nonexistent object key → Err
   - Test: forward reference (result_of of a later call) → Err
   - Test: reference to error response → Err
   - Test: escaped path ~1 in key name resolves correctly

2. Error formatting tests (oracles from RFC 8620 §7.1):
   - Verify error_invocation produces [method_name, {type:X,...}, call_id] format
   - Verify RequestError serializes to correct HTTP status + JSON body
   - Verify all error_type strings are exactly 'invalidArguments', 'unknownMethod', 'forbiddenMethod', 'accountNotFound', 'serverFail', 'unknownCapability', 'invalidResultReference'
   - Verify description omitted when None

3. E2E integration test:
   - Construct a multi-method JmapRequest with a valid ResultReference
   - Run parse_request → resolve_references → (stub dispatch) → JmapResponse
   - Verify response format, sessionState present, all call_ids echoed
   - Oracle: manually constructed from RFC 8620 §3 request/response examples

Defensive programming rules:
- All test expected values hand-crafted from RFC spec, never from code under test
- Tests must cover the REJECTION paths, not just happy paths
- No mocking of the resolver itself; test with real resolve_references function

Agent team: Single Tester agent. Tester derives all expected values from RFC 8620 before looking at implementation.
